name: Phenelzine
drug_class: Monoamine oxidase inhibitor (MAOI), irreversible non-selective hydrazine
route_note: Oral tablets in divided doses, with dietary tyramine restriction.

discovery.note: A hydrazine MAO inhibitor developed after iproniazid revealed the antidepressant potential of MAO inhibition in the 1950s. Year its synthesis was first described, by Emil Votoček and Otakar Leminger.

tagline: Irreversible MAO inhibitor kept for atypical and treatment-resistant depression
summary: Phenelzine is an irreversible, non-selective monoamine oxidase inhibitor of the hydrazine class. It is effective in atypical and treatment-resistant depression but requires dietary restrictions and careful drug-interaction management because of the risk of hypertensive crisis and serotonin syndrome.
mechanism: Phenelzine irreversibly inhibits MAO-A and MAO-B, preventing breakdown of serotonin, noradrenaline and dopamine and increasing their stores and release. Recovery requires synthesis of new enzyme over about two weeks.

Inhibition of intestinal and hepatic MAO-A allows dietary tyramine to reach the circulation and release noradrenaline, causing hypertensive reactions (the 'cheese reaction'). Phenelzine also raises brain GABA by inhibiting GABA transaminase.
uses: Depression, especially atypical, non-endogenous or treatment-resistant depression

history.title: Iproniazid
history.detail: The tuberculosis drug iproniazid is observed to elevate mood, leading to the MAOI class.

history.title: Psychic energiser
history.detail: Nathan Kline reports iproniazid as an antidepressant.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Phenelzine is approved in the US as Nardil.

history.title: Cheese reaction
history.detail: Hypertensive crises linked to tyramine-rich foods are described with MAOIs.

history.title: Suicidality warning
history.detail: Class boxed warning on suicidality in young people.

pk.half_life: About 11–12 hours (effect lasts weeks owing to irreversible inhibition)

serious: Hypertensive crisis with tyramine or sympathomimetics
safety.boxed_warning: Increased risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviours in children, adolescents and young adults (under 25) taking antidepressants; monitor for clinical worsening.

facts: A washout of at least two weeks is required when switching between phenelzine and most other antidepressants (five weeks after fluoxetine).
